idiom_name: typed context struct + askama Template derive (HTML) or serde_json (JSON) per channel
implementation_notes: Stage one is a Rust struct or enum owning the logical page; because the type is the contract, a renderer cannot reach past the fields it declares. Stage two is the per-channel renderer: deriving askama's Template turns that struct into a render()/Display implementation whose template is compiled and type-checked at build time (referencing a field the struct lacks fails the build), while deriving Serialize and calling serde_json::to_string renders the same value as JSON. Rust has no XSLT processor worth adopting, so the second stage is code rather than a stylesheet; use a runtime engine (minijinja, tera) only when templates must change without a rebuild.
pitfalls: askama resolves templates and fields at compile time, so a template edit needs a rebuild - per-tenant templates require a runtime engine instead.
Auto-escaping follows the template extension/derive, so rendering an HTML template into a text channel keeps HTML entities; one renderer per channel is required.
Two structs with the same fields drift: derive both traits on one type, or generate both renderers from one definition, so a new field cannot reach only one channel.
